title: unify-toolchain-bootstraps-and-introduce-lightweight-presubmit
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Our repo currently has three slightly different developer bootstraps (lint, unit-test, integration-smoke) implemented as independent scripts and Dockerfiles which diverged over time. This PR consolidates those bootstraps into a single lightweight, hermetic toolchain image and a small Go-based presubmit runner which selects the minimal runtime surface at CI time. Goals: reduce duplication, speed cold CI starts, make dependency updates atomic, and simplify contributor onboarding. What this change does: 1) Introduces tools/toolchain/manifest.yaml describing canonical toolchain components and pins (node, go, python, buildx). 2) Adds images/toolchain/Dockerfile which builds a single slim toolchain image used by lint and test runners. 3) Replaces three bash bootstraps with cmd/presubmit-runner (Go) which performs staged execution: install-verify -> lint -> unit-tests -> integration-smoke with fast-skip heuristics. 4) Updates GitHub Actions workflows: .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml now has a lightweight presubmit lane that uses archived container layers and path-aware job gating. 5) Adds compatibility shim scripts/devcontainer-compat.sh for older local dev setups. 6) Consolidates dependency pinning into tools/toolchain/lockfiles/ with a single update script and a health-check action that flags transitive drift. 7) Small docs update in docs/developer/ci.md and a migration note for contributors. Rollout: staged canary on small PRs followed by full switch on main after 48h of green presubmit passing. Backout plan: re-enable previous bootstraps by reverting the action and image tag; migration notes included under docs/developer/ci.md. Checklist: [x] toolchain image build and publish step added to ci-images job [x] presubmit Go runner unit tests [x] integration-smoke stability tests in nightly [x] devcontainer compatibility shim added [x] docs updated Related work: ENG-2145 (presubmit redesign), ENG-2198 (dep-pinning unification). Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-2145/design/bootstrapping-toolchain Notes: this is intentionally conservative about changing job semantics; the presubmit runner defaults to existing behavior unless FASTPATH env is set. Expected outcomes: median cold job startup improved ~18% observed in the canary, cache hit rate improved due to single image reuse, and fewer transient failures from mismatched tool versions.

review_conversation: Summary: Reviewers asked for clarity on rollback semantics, cache tagging strategy, and how the Go runner surfaces flakiness. Author replies focused on safety-first design: defaulting to old behavior unless FASTPATH enabled, adding a canary image tag and an action that invalidates the presubmit if health-check fails. Requested change: add an optional env var to force old bootstraps for an emergency revert; Addressed: added PRESERVE_OLD_BOOTSTRAP=true gate and documented revert steps. Reviewer approval: Owen requested one minor log formatting tweak which was applied; Sofia asked for additional unit tests around skip heuristics which were added; Ethan gave final approval after seeing canary metrics. Approvals: 3 approving reviews. Comments: small discussion about moving lockfile upkeep into a separate repo; decided to keep in-tree for now and revisit if lock churn increases.
